paper_title: Open X-Embodiment: Robotic Learning Datasets and RT-X Models
mechanism: A large transformer policy (RT-X) is pretrained on a heterogeneous mixture of robot demonstration datasets spanning 22 embodiments, then fine-tuned or evaluated on target robots. Cross-embodiment co-training exposes the model to diverse motor behaviors, object interactions, and visual contexts; the shared transformer backbone learns action-relevant features that transfer across morphologies. Improvement over single-robot baselines is driven by dataset diversity supplying gradient signal for generalizable sensorimotor representations, not by any single dataset's scale alone.
invariant: A model trained on sufficiently diverse behavioral data generalizes better than one trained on homogeneous data at equal or even larger scale — diversity of context acts as an implicit regularizer that suppresses overfitting to embodiment-specific or task-specific spurious correlations.
prediction: RT-X fine-tuned on a target robot outperforms a model trained only on that robot's own data, and ablating cross-embodiment data while holding total data volume constant degrades target-robot success rate — falsifiable by comparing the two training regimes on held-out real-robot tasks.
failure_mode: When a target embodiment's action space or morphology is too dissimilar from all training embodiments, shared representations do not transfer; the cross-embodiment benefit vanishes and co-training may even hurt by diluting relevant gradient signal with irrelevant trajectories.
